sample.title: How Meta Will Enforce New Age And Time Limits On Instagram And Facebook
sample.description:
Meta has agreed to pay up to $17 billion and make sweeping changes to Instagram and Facebook as part of a landmark child safety settlement with nearly every U.S. state. The deal introduces new protections for teens, including time limits, overnight blocks and stronger age verification, changes that could fundamentally alter how young people use Meta’s platforms. But implementing those safeguards, particularly determining users’ ages, presents major technical and business challenges. CNBC’s Julia Boorstin examines how Meta plans to pull it off, and why the settlement could ultimately force changes across TikTok, YouTube and the rest of the social media industry.

sample.title: Anthropic’s Distillation Battle Turns To The Dark Web As China Concerns Swell
sample.description:
Foreign companies have allegedly been accessing American AI systems to train competing technology — a process called distillation — and selling copycat versions at a lower price. Anthropic is trying to crack down on what it says are illegal practices that involve use of the dark web and intellectual property theft. Jacob Klein, Anthropic's head of threat intelligence, says, "there's an entire illicit ecosystem to try to gain access to Claude and other models.” CNBC's Kate Rooney has the story.

sample.title: Crypto Bet Big On U.S. Regulation, And Now Its Landmark Legislation Hangs In The Balance
sample.description:
The crypto industry's biggest legislative bet is being put to the test as Congress prepares to return from its August recess. Lobbyists and lawmakers are sifting through the Clarity Act in hopes of passing the comprehensive crypto rulebook before the midterm elections. But the industry is signaling waning confidence that the bill will pass, and is instead looking to other agencies like the SEC and CFTC to regulate the industry without Clarity.

Why is the next Silent Hill set in Scotland? | BBC News
sample.description:
Silent Hill, the psychological survival horror franchise from Japanese studio Konami, has for the most part been set in America, although the most recent excursion - Silent Hill f - was based in Japan in the 1960s era.
 
Now in Silent Hill Townfall, made by the Glasgow-based team Screen Burn, that location is in an entirely new place - Scotland, albeit a fictional part of it - St Amelia. Scotland was initially going to be more of an influence than a setting, but the team ultimately decided to embrace it fully.
 
Director Jon McKellan spoke to BBC Tech Now's Laura Cress at Gamescom, Cologne.

sample.description:
It has been just over two weeks since a crash on the A66 duel carriageway near Middlesborough, which killed seven people - including two police officers.
 
The BBC's Ed Thomas has travelled to the Grangetown area of the city, which, along with the South Bank area, has been the focus of a large police operation into organised crime following the tragedy.
 
Speaking exclusively to the BBC, Cleveland Police's Chief Constable Victoria Fuller has said she is proud of her "brave" force but that it was being "let down" by the way it was funded, following the fatal crash. 
 
She said her officers are dealing with some of the highest crime levels in the country akin to those faced by metropolitan forces, but with less than half the number of officers.

sample.title: Human poo and maggot-infested food left behind at beauty spot. #Wales #BBCNews
Lindsay Clancy murder trial collapses as jurors fail to reach verdict | BBC News
sample.description:
The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial has declared a mistrial after jurors said they could not reach a unanimous verdict on whether she was criminally responsible when she strangled her three young children. The ruling, reached after seven days of deliberations, leaves the case unresolved and allows prosecutors to try Clancy again.

The final day of the trial took a dramatic turn when the judge gave Clancy’s attorney a chance to appeal the mistrial order. Her lawyer was angry that a note from the jury had suggested that a single juror wouldn’t follow the court’s instructions about reasonable doubt. The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court ultimately denied the appeal.

Clancy, a 36-year-old former labor and delivery nurse, doesn’t deny strangling her children in the basement of their home in 2023. Clancy’s legal team has argued that postpartum psychosis led to her actions, while prosecutors say she knew what she was doing.

Clive Myrie presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Ione Wells in Massachusetts.
